biggest_catch: ProZ.com never pays translators a cent — every dollar comes from a client you win yourself, so the '$1,000' figure is just illustrative of freelance income, never a ProZ payout.
catches: ProZ does not pay translators; it is a directory/marketplace — you must find clients, agree your own rate, and get paid by them directly.
Zero guaranteed jobs: income depends entirely on your profile, bids, and winning work; competition is global.
Rates are set by you and vary wildly by language pair and specialization — there is no standard ProZ rate.
Payment terms (method, net days) are negotiated per client; ProZ's own scam-alert center advises demanding a purchase order and exact payment terms up front.
A paid membership tier exists for full job-board/directory access (optional, not required to register) — treat membership cost as a business expense.
ProZ*Pay is only an optional payout channel (Wise/PayPal/Payoneer/Skrill), not a guarantee of payment.

c1.evidence: ProZ.com is the largest real operating translation marketplace/directory (proz.com, founded 1999); official blog at go.proz.com loaded.

c2.evidence: Official ProZ materials state the model plainly: translators create profiles, bid on jobs posted by outsourcers, set their own rates, and agree payment terms directly with the client. ProZ*Pay is an optional payout channel ('ProZ*Pay has been built for the language community to speed up payments... help freelancers keep more money').

c3.evidence: Registration is free; optional paid membership for full features is a subscription, not a condition of being paid.

c4.evidence: No fixed pay figure exists — ProZ explicitly publishes no rates (translators set their own). The pay MECHANISM is verified: client → translator directly per agreed terms, optionally via ProZ*Pay (Wise, PayPal, Payoneer, Skrill). payout_quote is null since there is no official rate.

eligibility: Anyone can register free and build a translator profile; to win work you need demonstrable language skills, stated rates per language pair, and competitive bids on posted jobs. Optional paid membership unlocks full job-board/directory features.
notes: Read official ProZ sources (2026-09-22): the ProZ blog article 'How freelance translators get paid in USD using Wise (formerly Transferwise), PayPal, Payoneer, Skrill and more' (go.proz.com) documents ProZ*Pay as an optional payout channel for receiving client payments; the ProZ risk-management/scam-alert page (proz.com/about/translator-scam-alerts/risk-management) instructs translators to 'Agree on clear terms and conditions ... the payment method and payment terms' and request a purchase order with 'exact payment terms (how many days after your invoice you will be paid and by which method)' — confirming payment flows client-to-translator, not through ProZ. The catalog's '$1,000' claim is not a ProZ-published payout and cannot be verified; it is treated as an illustrative earnings figure. No commits, no DB writes.

s1.note: No fixed eligibility bar — skill, profile quality, and bidding determine who gets work; optional paid membership tiers exist.

s2.note: You set your own rates; clients choose translators by profile/reviews; payment terms negotiated per client (ProZ advises a written purchase order).

s3.note: Timing is whatever you agree with each client (e.g., net 15/30/45); ProZ does not process the payment — ProZ*Pay is only an optional channel.

s4.note: ProZ makes no earnings promises itself — honest that income is self-determined; the '$1,000' catalog figure is not official.

s6.note: Steps are concrete: free profile → set rates → bid on jobs → agree written terms (purchase order) → deliver → invoice → paid directly by the client (optionally via ProZ*Pay).

s7.note: Official ProZ blog and proz.com risk-management page read 2026-09-22.

steps: Register a free account on proz.com and build your translator profile (language pairs, specializations, and your own rates).
Browse the translation jobs board and submit competitive bids on posted jobs, or get found via the translator directory.

Before starting work, agree on clear written terms with the client: scope, exact total cost/rate, delivery date, payment method, and how many days after invoice you are paid (request a purchase order).
Deliver the translation, then invoice the client per the agreed terms — the client pays you directly, not ProZ.
Optionally receive client payments via ProZ*Pay (Wise, PayPal, Payoneer, or Skrill) to speed up payouts and cut conversion fees.
Optionally take a paid ProZ membership for full job-board and directory visibility, treating it as a business cost.
timing: Per-client terms you negotiate (e.g., net 15/30/45 after invoice); ProZ does not set or process payment timing.
